title: The before-and-after check's proof fixes: a release waits off staging for its before look, and no wrong note when its look comes in; the Staging page's status l
why: Release #304, 2026-11-26, the first release through the before-and-after check, found three faults. (1) The 10-minute release job put #304 on staging at 11:00 while its before look ran from 10:46 to 11:13 (Releases::tick moves on any git build left at Planned for 10 minutes), so half the before look was of staging with the change already on. Now the job leaves a release that BeforeAfter is waiting on (phase before) alone; BeforeAfter::step puts it on staging once its look is in. (2) When the look came in, BeforeAfter::step called the staging step again on a release already staged, and "its plan needs a look: Its plan was approved already. Approve it on System Configuration → Releases." was written on it as a person's task; now a release already on staging goes straight to its after look. (3) Both staff test logins couldn't sign in, so no admin page was checked as staff, and #304, admin only, read pass: the verdict rule is in tools/page-audit/beforeafter.mjs, already in main (#1433) (an account that alone checks a kind of page failing while the change names such a page makes the look incomplete, a person looks). Admin only, no table, no outside call. Also (Jason's screenshot, 2026-11-26, after Try again): the Staging page's redraw after a press (admin-staging.js) set the section's HTML again without TvAsk.statuses, so the Now line and "Outside calls that skip the gate" came back as bare text with no box or label; now the redraw draws them as the page does.
